reasonToGo: Clintlack lies at the far end of the eastern road, three and four stages of cart beyond the port, on the shore of a basin of enclosed water the sea does not reach. That distance decides what leaves: garden ground on the river islands feeds the two villages rather than the port, and only the squarest slab and the best-picked ore are worth putting on a cart at all.

hazards.name: The channel behind
hazards.description: The river lays its load down in a fan of channels and does not keep any of them. A strip that was walked onto dry in the morning has moving water behind it by afternoon, carrying whatever the flood upstream has already picked up, and the people on it are on an island nobody made.

hazards.name: The passage fall
hazards.description: The roof of the workings under the tower comes away in plates along the bedding, without warning and without much noise. A plate the size of a door is enough to put a loaded man face down on the floor of a passage he then has to be dragged out of.

resources.name: Island garden
resources.description: Worked in strips on the silt islands between the river's channels, between one flood and the next, and eaten by the two villages here rather than carted anywhere. What the road takes out is heavy; food is what stays.

resources.name: Clintlack tower ore
resources.description: Got from the workings driven in under the tower, where the ore lies in the rock the water left rather than on the face of it, and sorted at the mouth before it ever sees a basket.

resources.name: Carted slab
resources.description: Split in flat slabs off the pavement beside the road and loaded onto the carts coming back up empty from the villages. A slab that will not lie flat in a cart is left where it was split, and the road is edged with them.

landmarks.name: Paveshaft Geo
landmarks.description: A slot the sea has cut back into the cliff along a weak seam, working further into the rock every winter and taking the ground above it as it goes. Carters walk their beasts past it rather than drive them.

landmarks.name: Pot at Limerake
landmarks.description: The hole a surface stream walks into on the high ground and does not come back out of. Carters water their beasts above it, because below it the stream is not there to be found.
